text: The switch flip is one function but changes the contract in three places at once: resolveTransport default, the module header's default-and-fallback sentence, and the cli-jev SKILL switch table; the 038 switch-off byte recordings stop being the running baseline.

A default path pays runtime construction and the model/credential gates per call unless cached; the measured 260 ms mean is the benchmark's once-per-run runtime, and the transport itself has never made a live call.

Default-on needs identity pinning first: the Pi gate resolves any version while the verdict is scoped to Pi 0.99.1 and a new identity must rerun the keep rule; the CLI gate already pins jev 0.6.2 and skips on mismatch.

Default-on needs quiet fallback semantics: on a machine without Pi credentials or package a skip line would print on every call, turning a diagnostic into noise; either quiet-by-default or a once-per-process preflight.

Cost moved by default-on is small and metered: about $0.0022/100 calls, ~$0.0075 per 333-call replay, $0 at the unmeasured free arm; the CLI side records no cost, so the flip trades unrecorded for metered spend.
The failure path doubles worst-case latency: a failed, timed-out or gate-stopped Pi attempt is followed by the full CLI call, with no circuit breaker and no retry inside the transport.
Observability must land before a default: callers write backend jev even when Pi answers, usage is unrecorded, and dispatch auditing stops seeing the judgment once it does not leave the process.

The verdict is the first risk: adopt vs keep-cli is one row of 111 with overlapping CIs ([89.8,98.5] vs [88.6,98.0]); a default flip inherits a noisy 95.5 unless measured wider, repeated same-day, or explicitly accepted.

Data path changes for every caller: CLI asks official jev-1.13.0, Pi asks typesafe/jev-1.13 through OpenRouter; a default-on decision moves every prompt to a third-party gateway and a different credential store.

Blast radius is bounded today (two require sites, Hermes mirrors skill-only) and grows with adoption; a staged auto mode that prefers Pi when gates pass, quiet otherwise, is safer than a hard default change.

Default-on is defensible only as a monitored commitment: pin identities in the gate, rerun the keep rule on identity change, keep the CLI fallback and an escape value, and record backend/usage per call so the default stays auditable.
